info.name: Insuredmine Policy Import API
info.description: Complete collection for the Node.js policy-import assessment. Every API response uses success, statusCode, message, data, and optional meta/errors fields. Select a local file in the upload request before sending it.

request.description: Checks only whether the API process is alive.

exec: pm.test('Response uses the success envelope', () => { pm.expect(body.success).to.eql(true); pm.expect(body.statusCode).to.eql(200); pm.expect(body.message).to.be.a('string'); });

request.description: Requires MongoDB and Redis to be connected.

exec: pm.test('Response uses the success envelope', () => { pm.expect(body.success).to.eql(true); pm.expect(body.statusCode).to.eql(200); });

request.description: Shows sampled Node.js process CPU percentage, CPU restart threshold, memory usage, uptime, and whether automatic restart is enabled. CPU is sampled every five seconds after the API starts.

exec: pm.test('CPU metrics use the standard response envelope', () => { pm.expect(body.success).to.eql(true); pm.expect(body.statusCode).to.eql(200); pm.expect(body.data.processCpuPercent === null || typeof body.data.processCpuPercent === 'number').to.eql(true); });

request.description: Body → form-data → choose your file for key `file`. Supported extensions are .csv and .xlsx. The response is asynchronous; use Get Import Status until status is completed, failed, or duplicate.

exec: pm.test('Response uses the success envelope', () => { pm.expect(body.success).to.eql(true); pm.expect(body.statusCode).to.eql(202); });

request.description: Reads row totals, skipped/duplicate counts, errors, headers, file audit metadata, and final import status from response.data.

item.name: Search policy information by first name or email

query.description: Use only for a case-insensitive prefix search. Example: jay returns Jay, Jayesh, etc.
Use only for a case-insensitive partial email search. Example: @gmail.com. Do not send with firstName.

request.description: Provide exactly one search parameter. firstName performs a case-insensitive prefix search (jay → Jay, Jayesh); email performs a case-insensitive partial search (@gmail.com). Sending firstName and email together returns HTTP 400. Policies are in response.data and pagination/search information is in response.meta.

Returns paginated policy count and total premium per user. Data is in response.data; total, page, limit, and totalPages are in response.meta. page defaults to 1 and limit defaults to 20 (maximum 100).
Redis and npm run worker:messages must be running. The explicit +05:30 offset avoids timezone ambiguity.
Backward-compatible input. It uses the server's local timezone, so prefer the ISO request above.
